walkthroughs.body_html:
Coasts are dynamic and changing:

• Erosion destroys homes and roads
• Flooding from storm surges
• Sea-level rise from climate change

We must balance protection vs cost vs nature.

Hard engineering uses built structures:
• Sea walls, groynes, rip-rap
• Effective but expensive and ugly

Soft engineering works with nature:
• Beach nourishment, dune planting
• Cheaper, more sustainable

UK Shoreline Management Plans pick from 4 options:

1. Hold the line (defend)
2. Advance the line (build out)
3. Managed retreat (let it flood)
4. Do nothing

Choice depends on cost-benefit analysis.

options: Beach nourishment
Sea wall
Dune planting
Managed retreat
Sediment moving along the coast
Cliff retreat
Sea-level rise
Tidal flooding
Longshore drift is the rising of sea level over time.
Longshore drift carries sediment past a change in coastline direction (e.g. river mouth); deposition continues into deeper water, building a curved depositional landform with a hook.
A spit is a small island just off the coast.
A spit forms where the river deposits its sediment at the coast.

mcqs.q: What drives the movement of tectonic plates?
options: Convection currents in the mantle combined with slab pull at subduction zones and ridge push at constructive boundaries.
Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
Longshore drift is the rising of sea level over time.
The Earth's rotation makes the plates move.
